newsitem.title: USA: Pioneer Financial sells managed healthcare segment.
newsitem.headline: Pioneer Financial sells managed healthcare segment.

text.p: Pioneer Financial Services Inc said Friday it sold its managed healthcare subsidiary, National Health Services Inc, to United Payors & United Providers Inc for cash consideration and warrants.
Pioneer Financial also said the stock of ACMG Inc, another small healthcare management subsidiary, was repurchased by its former shareholder group.
The value of the deals was not given.

Pioneer said its managed care division was the smallest of its business units, with 1995 revenue of $17.1 milion and pre-tax income of $739,000. It said the sale will not have a material impact on income.

"The sale of (National Health Services) and ACMG will allow us to better focus our efforts on our three major business divisions: health and life insurance for senior citizens, medical coverage for small busiensses and the self-employed, and life insurance for middle-income individuals," Peter Nauert, chairman, said in a statement.
Pioneer said it bought National Health in 1990 to enhance managed care services for its health insurance operations.
"We will maintain the contracts we have with (National Health) to provide utilization review and case management for our health insurance companies," Nauert said.
Through its relationship with United Payors, Pioneer Financial said it expects to continue expanding its managed care programs.
Pioneer Financial purchased ACMG in mid-1995, with an objective to develop health maintenance organizations (HMOs) in selected geographic areas.

"However, over the last year, we have determined that we cannot develop HMOs to be competitive with larger companies," Nauert said. "The large HMOs have been aggressively pricing their services to dynamically increase market share."

As a result, Pioneer Financial has decided to concentrate its efforts and capital on its insurance operations through development and marketing of exclusive provider organizations (EPO) plans. "We expect to have a greater return on these plans than on the HMOs we had considered developing," Nauert said.
